lessons.question: Your Bot shows a polished follow-up email to a customer. Has the customer received it?
options: Yes, the Bot finished the task
Not necessarily, a draft is not a sent message
Only if the email mentions the customer by name
lessons.explanation: Reviewing the output as work means telling a draft follow-up apart from a message already sent. In this exercise every proposed action should still be a draft.

lessons.after: Make the result explicit: a draft brief
lessons.prompt: Which of these belong in the Bot's explicit result for this exercise?
lessons.explanation: A clear, reviewable artifact is the goal. Real accounts stay disconnected, and agents in the Harbour case may draft but never contact customers.

lessons.question: You write never export files into a Bot's personal instruction. How should you describe that control?
options: A guarantee covering every Bot on the account
A communicated rule, not an enforced boundary
lessons.explanation: A personal instruction tells the Bot your rule but does not enforce it. Some organisational enforcement needs Enterprise access, so describe controls by what is actually available.

lessons.after: Open the generated artifact, check the source
lessons.prompt: Mid-task, a website asks for a sign-in before the Bot can continue. What do you do?
lessons.answer: Perform that authorised step yourself. Never paste credentials into the conversation for the Bot to use.

lessons.prompt: A report runs by itself every Monday. List three ways a run could go wrong without anyone noticing.
lessons.answer: The input is missing, a connection has expired, or the data has not refreshed. A good routine reports that condition rather than producing a plausible report from stale memory.

lessons.after: After a successful manual run, follow the
lessons.prompt: Put the life of a test routine in order.
steps: Specify source, window rule, timezone, destination and review owner
Inspect the result and run history
Pause the routine at the end of the exercise
lessons.explanation: Automate only work that already succeeds by hand, check the first run's evidence, and leave nothing running when the exercise ends.

lessons.after: Run the common brief through OpenClaw, Hermes
lessons.prompt: In the three-system comparison, what do you hold fixed and what do you record as it varies?
lessons.explanation: Fixing inputs, rubric and date makes the systems comparable. Measures like review time and permissions are the results you are comparing.

lessons.question: One platform scores best on your five cases. What can you honestly claim?
options: Its underlying model is the strongest
That complete system did best on your cases
It will win for every business task
lessons.explanation: You could not force the same model everywhere, so the result describes whole systems as tested. Record the limitation alongside the outcome.

lessons.question: Could no deployment ever be the right recommendation after comparing three platforms?
options: No, you should always pick the top scorer
Only if every platform failed to install
Yes, if no option fits the business task
lessons.explanation: The business route allows recommending a platform, a simpler workflow or no deployment. The choice follows the task, not a general product ranking.

lessons.after: Configure one Bot with fictional inputs
lessons.prompt: Step 5: one platform gave you no log measurement. Why not fill the gap with a reasonable estimate?
lessons.answer: An estimate disguised as an observation corrupts the comparison. The gap is itself evidence about that platform, so label it as missing.

lessons.after: Define who receives and reviews the report
lessons.question: The routine runs on a cloud computer. Which is an adequate stop plan?
options: Closing the application on your laptop
A reviewed stop procedure using the routine controls
Renaming the Bot so it is easy to find
lessons.explanation: Cloud work can keep running after your app closes. The business route reviews the routine configuration and stop procedure so stopping is deliberate and checkable.

lessons.prompt: Which factors can be traded off, and which rule a platform out if they fail?

items.text: Being able to stop the work

lessons.explanation: A high average cannot compensate for a mandatory permission failure. The Week 11 gate asks you to demonstrate access boundaries and stopping work.
